To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The catalytic domain of the human macrophage metalloelastase (MME) was successfully expressed in Escherichia coli and purified to >95% homogeneity; (2) The recombinant enzyme was stable at room temperature and could be stored at 4 degrees C for several months; (3) The enzyme exhibited a high degree of sequence homology with other human matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), but had distinct biochemical properties;

(1) the human macrophage metalloelastase catalytic domain (MMECD) was expressed in a soluble and active form in the cytoplasm of Escherichia coli; and (2) the recombinant MMECD was purified to homogeneity by a single chromatographic step, and was used for the screening of inhibitors of MMECD activity.
